1) polar bears in two adjacent subpoputions varied their activity levels in three habitat types; 2) the subpopulation that has experienced a greater decline in habitat availability has exhibited greater declines in activity; and 3) bears alter their activity levels in response to changes in habitat conditions.

polar bears in both the SB and CS subpopulations are responding to habitat changes by changing their behavior, and this is likely to have negative consequences for their long-term survival.

the polar bear population in the Southern Beafort sea is experiencing a significant decline in the number of bears due to the loss of habitat and prey.

behavioral changes in response to environmental change are important to consider when forecasting species’ responses to climate change, particularly for species that are not well adapted to the new conditions.
